shipped.title_o: Children's acquisition of the number words and the counting system
shipped.outcome_quote: Results showed that acquiring the cardinal meanings of number words spread out over a protracted period, far more extended than assumed by Wynn.

blind_target.title: Children's acquisition of the number words and the counting system
blind_target.evidence_quote: The present work focused on the GaN from Wynn's (1990Wynn's ( , 1992) ) studies with no intention to test the replicability of results coming from the other tasks (i.e., the Point-to-x task or the colour control task were not administered).
blind_target.outcome_quote: A second issue concerned the age of acquisition of cardinal knowledge. Wynn (1992) claimed that children become CP-knowers around 3 ½ year-old (42 months) and reported an effect of age suggesting that younger children exhibit lower level of cardinal knowledge (one-, two-and three-knowers) than older children. A similar correlation between age and cardinal knowledge was indeed observed in Study 1. However, convergent observations from Study 1 and 2 indicates that cardinal knowledge were far from achieving maturity at the age of 3 ½ years.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly report agreement with some original observations and disagreement with others; no overall replication verdict supersedes those comparisons.

shipped.title_o: Should We Pay for Our Social Media/Messenger Applications? Preliminary Data on the Acceptance of an Alternative to the Current Prevailing Data Business Model
shipped.outcome_quote: The results showed that the willingness to pay for these services was significantly higher in 2022 compared to the results published in 2020.

blind_target.authors: Sindermann C., Kuss D.J., Throuvala M.A., Griffiths M.D., Montag C.
blind_target.title: Should we pay for our social media/messenger applications? Preliminary data on the acceptance of an alternative to the current prevailing data business model.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Given the significant changes in social media platforms between 2020 and 2022 and the increased number of users [ 53 ], we recognized the importance of replicating the study conducted by Sindermann et al. in Q1 2020 with our study conducted in Q4 2022, accumulating to almost three years.
blind_target.outcome_quote: The results of Comparison 2, i.e., between Germans in 2020 and Germans 2022, suggested that there are differences in users' interest in willingness to pay for social media for digital wellbeing. Specifically, the total score of user willingness to pay for social media platforms was higher in 2022 compared to 2020. Furthermore, there was a significant difference in participants’ interest towards data protection, usage not prolonged, and fake news and radicalism reduction. However, the monthly amount participants were willing to pay for messenger services was higher in 2020. The results for Comparison 3 replicated the outcome of Comparison 2 except for data protection and the amount of monthly messenger fee, where the difference between Germans 2020 vs. Germans and Europeans 2022 was insignificant.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors report changed total willingness and several service scores compared with 2020, alongside unchanged other service scores and monthly fees. No overall confirmation/failure verdict is stated; mixed reflects explicit comparisons, with uncertainty because this is principally a temporal-change study.

shipped.title_o: ERN and the placebo: A misattribution approach to studying the arousal properties of the error-related negativity.
shipped.outcome_quote: ERN/Ne differences between misattribution and control group could not be replicated, although the statistical power of the replication study was high.

blind_target.title: ERN and the placebo: a misattribution approach to studying the arousal properties of the error-related negativity.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Therefore, the aim of the present study was to investigate whether an experimental manipulation of the misattribution of state-anxiety following errors modulates the ERN/Ne. To this end, we aimed at replicating the findings of Inzlicht and Al-Khindi (2012).
blind_target.outcome_quote: As Inzlicht and Al-Khindi (2012), we did not observe performance differences between both groups. However, ERN/Ne differences between misattribution and control group could not be replicated, although the statistical power of the replication study was high. Evidence regarding the replication of performance and the non-replication of ERN/Ne findings was confirmed by Bayesian statistics.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Explicit comparison confirms the original null performance finding but fails the ERN/Ne effect. The introduction expressly says replication of the null performance result is as important as replication of the ERN/Ne result; thus both are planned target findings. There is no overall verdict overriding these contrasting comparisons. The terminology reproducibility refers here to a new sample, not reanalysis of original data.

shipped.title_o: Implicit attitudes towards native and non-native speaker teachers
shipped.outcome_quote: students' implicit and explicit attitudes towards NESTs have become more positive in the ten years since the original study

blind_target.authors: Watson Todd, R. and Pojanapunya. P.
blind_target.title: Implicit attitudes towards native and non-native speaker teachers.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
The purpose of this study, then, is to replicate Watson Todd and Pojanapunya (2009) to see
if changes in the sociolinguistic context have influenced attitudes towards NESTs and LETs in
Thailand.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
From Table 3, we can see that the previous explicit preference for NESTs has remained
unchanged, the previous warmer feelings towards LETs have now become neutral, and the previous
lack of any implicit preference has now become a weak implicit preference for NESTs. Overall, it
appears that there has been a shift in attitudes of all types in favour of NESTs.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly retain the original explicit preference for NESTs but contrast the original warmer feelings towards LETs and absent implicit preference with new neutral feelings and weak implicit NEST preference. These are partial agreement and partial disagreement with the published findings. Failure of their new temporal-change expectation is not itself a replication outcome.

shipped.title_o: Do State‐Customized TANF Work Policies Actually Reduce Unemployment?*
shipped.outcome_quote: Kim and Berry's research seemingly contains significant flaws, including incorrect results. This replication project offers evidence that the significant decrease in unemployment among low-income females is likely not present, highlighting the importance of documentation and replication.

blind_target.authors: Kim, Na Yeon, and Berry, Frances Stokes
blind_target.title: Do State‐Customized TANF Work Policies Actually Reduce Unemployment?
blind_target.evidence_quote: The original purpose of this project was to expand on Kim and Berry's research regarding TANF policies. Methods I created a dataset that closely matched Kim and Berry's original dataset.
blind_target.outcome_computational_quote: The inclusion of fixed effects and trend variables, which Kim and Berry reported using in their model, caused the WSP variable to become about 0 percent and insignificant.
blind_target.outcome_robustness_quote: The results of the synthetic control methods provided additional evidence that questions the validity of the original findings.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Reconstructs the original observational dataset and applies its reported model, which produces materially different numbers; alternative synthetic-control analyses also challenge the original conclusion. Original reference list unavailable, so year and DOI are unreported and names/title are taken from the abstract.
